title: Backend Engineer - Storage Systems
description:
JOIN PROTON AND BUILD A BETTER INTERNET WHERE PRIVACY IS THE DEFAULT

At Proton, we believe that privacy is a fundamental human right and the cornerstone of democracy. Since our inception in 2014, founded by a team of scientists from CERN, we have dedicated ourselves to providing free and open-source technology to millions worldwide, ensuring access to privacy, security, and freedom online.

Our journey began with Proton Mail, the largest secure email service globally, and has since expanded to include Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive, and Proton Pass.

Proton is a profitable company, supporting over 100 million user accounts with a growing team of over 500 people from over 50 different countries, from the world's top companies and universities.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Storage is at the very center of everything we do. Whatever needs to be persisted eventually uses our Storage infrastructure. For this we run our storage infrastructure predominantly on-premise in multiple data centers. In this role you will join the Storage Dev team that is responsible to develop and maintain all the software required in the Storage realm. This, among others, includes Storage APIs, Seaweed & Ceph contributions.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Be responsible for the operational excellence of the systems/features and their interaction with other systems
- Work closely with a group of Back-End Engineers and Architects to build resilient, massively-scalable solutions for millions of people to rely on
- Collaborate with the SRE teams and other stakeholders to ensure that the Storage back-end meets critical business and reliability requirements
- Document back-end capabilities and their proper use
- Create technical designs and implement them to further develop the platform

JOB REQUIREMENTS

- Deep experience with Back-end development (C++, Go, Rust, or PHP)
- Experience building complex production systems
- Experience with profiling methods and tools
- Experience leading a team initiative from discovery to production
- Solid understanding of security best practices
- High-level understanding of cryptography concepts

BONUS POINTS FOR

- Experience with storage systems (e.g. Ceph, Seaweed or Tape)
- Operational experience such as SRE or on-call, demonstrating ability to diagnose and troubleshoot complex problems for critical systems

WHAT WE OFFER

Office Locations: Geneva, Zurich, Prague, Barcelona, Paris, London, Vilnius, Skopje, Taipei
- Work from home up to 30% of the time with three core days in the office
- Technology: All devices and software needed to excel
- Food: Lunch and snacks provided daily at offices
- Transport: Subsidized public transport, bike allowances, or parking spaces based on office location
- Stock Options: Everyone is an owner of the company
- Flexible Working: Define your own working hours (aligned with team meetings)
- Learning and Development: Training programs, conferences, events, continual learning
- Comprehensive health insurance plans
- Competitive retirement savings options
- Generous vacation and leave policies
- Wellness programs
- Work that Matters: 100 million+ users trust Proton; user subscriptions are our only revenue source

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

Proton believes diversity drives innovation. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical ability, or socio-economic background, feel valued and empowered.

ai_analysis.summary: This candidate presents exceptional low-level systems, C/C++/Rust, and Linux kernel programming skills highly relevant to storage infrastructure. However, the explicit requirement for 'deep experience building complex production systems' and 'leading a team initiative from discovery to production' poses a significant seniority mismatch for a first graduate role, critically impacting the overall fit for this specific Backend Engineer position.
resume_tips: Quantify the scale and impact of 'complex production systems' built in freelance roles to better align with production system requirements.
Elaborate on specific security best practices and cryptography concepts applied in projects or coursework, beyond just LUKS.
Reframe leadership experience to explicitly highlight managing technical initiatives from 'discovery to production' if applicable, even in academic contexts.
Highlight Rust experience more prominently in project descriptions or dedicated sections, as it's a key required language.
Emphasize any operational aspects or reliability considerations from projects to address the 'operational excellence' and 'SRE' bonus points.
